info.name: IPro — Mobile App API
info.description:
# IPro — Mobile App API

Everything the IPro mobile app needs, grouped by the Figma sections so a
folder matches the screens you are building.

## Before you start

Run **01 · Account › Sign in**. It stores `accessToken` for you and every
other request picks it up automatically. Nothing else to set up.

Test login: `devsushil25@gmail.com` / `12345678`

## Where baseUrl points

`https://sabbir2004.ssh.bd/api/v1` is a tunnel to the development machine,
not a hosted server. It answers only while that machine is running the
backend; when it is off you will get a **502**, which means "nobody is
listening", not "your request was wrong".

Running the backend yourself? Change the collection variable `baseUrl` to
`http://localhost:2004/api/v1`.

## The two rules that shape this API

**The paywall is the office.** A subscription unlocks offices, never levels
and never disciplines. Every plan includes all four levels (Beginner,
Intermediate, Advanced, Expert) and every discipline of the offices it
grants. Read what a user may open from `GET /subscription/my-access`:
`officeCodes` is the union of every plan they hold.

**A session is always 20 questions.** What changes with the level is the time
allowed: Beginner 20 min, Intermediate 30, Advanced 40, Expert 50. The only
exception is a pool with fewer than 20 questions, where the response carries
`isShortSession: true` and a `note` you should show the user.

## Profiles

At sign-up a user chooses **Paralegal** or **Attorney**. A paralegal never
sees a question marked Attorney — about 22% of the catalogue — so menus,
counts and pools all differ by profile. The demo asks for it before it
starts, since there is no account yet.

## Privacy

A user's profile picture is never visible to another user, anywhere. First
name and profession may be shared only if the user switches them on
(`PATCH /user/privacy-settings`), and both start off. Everything else —
surname, e-mail, phone, date of birth — is the user's alone. Use
`GET /user/public/:id` whenever you show one user to another.

## What is in the database right now

One office is imported: **IPI (Switzerland)**, 2,400 questions across 12
sheets — Patents, Trademarks and Designs, four levels each. The other
fourteen offices are listed by the catalogue with `isAvailable: false`
until their workbooks are imported, so a request for them answers "no
questions yet". That is correct behaviour, not a bug.

## Requests that change data

Most of this collection only reads. These do not — read the note on each
before sending, and do **not** use "Run collection" on the whole thing:

| Request | What it does |
|---|---|
| 01 · Sign up | creates a user |
| 01 · Change password | changes the password you signed in with |
| 01 · Sign out | invalidates the token |
| 02 · Update my profile | overwrites profile fields |
| 02 · Set profile type | changes which questions the user sees |
| 02 · Privacy settings — update | changes sharing |
| 02 · Delete my account | deletes the account |
| 03/04 · Submit a session | scores it and records mistakes |
| 06 · Choose offices | allowed once per billing period |
| 06 · Sync from RevenueCat | rewrites the user's subscriptions |
| 07 · Claim the 10% discount | issues a promo code |
| 10 · Send a report | files a real report for the content team |

request.description:
Creates the account and e-mails a 6-digit OTP. The account is not usable until **Verify OTP**.

`profileType` is the Paralegal / Attorney choice from the sign-up screen. It decides which questions this user will ever see, so ask for it before calling this.
Send the token returned by Sign up as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, and the 6 digits from the e-mail.
Returns `data.token`, a 15-minute reset token. Send it as the Bearer token on the next two calls — **not** the normal access token.
Bearer token = the reset token from the previous call.
Bearer token = the reset token. Screen: "Set New Password".
Figma: Settings › Change Password.
Reads the refreshToken cookie set at sign-in.

Figma: **login** section (5 screens) and the sign-up screens of **Demo quiz**.

Sign in first: it stores `accessToken` for the whole collection.

item.name: Profile & privacy

request.description: The signed-in user’s own record, in full.

**multipart/form-data**, not JSON — the route runs an upload handler.

Fields: `name`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `profession`, `email`, `phoneNumber`, and `profile` for the picture file. Do not set Content-Type by hand; let the client add the multipart boundary.
Decides the question pool for everything the user does. A paralegal never sees a question marked Attorney.

Both switches start **off**.

`neverShared` lists what cannot be shared at all, so the app does not have to hard-code the rule.
Only these two may ever be switched on. There is deliberately no flag for the picture, the surname or the e-mail.

What one user may see of another: first name and profession, and only where that user switched them on. Never the picture, never the e-mail.

Use this anywhere you show one user to another.
Figma: Settings › Delete Account.

item.description:
Figma: **Profile Section** (19 screens).

Privacy is a legal requirement here, not a preference: GDPR Art. 25(2) and
the Swiss DPA Art. 7. Nothing in a profile is visible to another user unless
that user switched it on, and the picture is never shareable at all.

item.name: Demo (no account)

request.description: All 15 offices with their disciplines, sheet counts and question counts, derived from the imported content. `isAvailable: false` means nothing is imported for that office yet — do not offer it.

Returns the 20 questions, already shuffled, **without the answer key**.

Each question carries the header line the screen needs: `office`, `discipline`, `level`, `theme`, `progress` ("7 / 20").
Closing the app suspends a session; this returns it with whatever was already ticked (`selectedKey`).
Send every question. `selectedKey: null` means left unanswered, which counts as wrong — and it still appears in the review with the correct answer.

Runs to the full 20, unanswered questions included.

Each question lists its four options **once each**, marking in place the one the user chose (`isChosen`) and the correct one (`isCorrect`), plus the explanation and the legal basis. The legal basis is text with no link — the workbooks carry no URL.

Works with or without a token. The office, sheet and Case_No are read from the stored question, so the content team can find the row in the workbook immediately.

Send either `question` (our id) or `questionId` (the readable one).

item.description:
Figma: **Demo quiz** section (20 screens).

Every request here works without a token. The demo asks "Paralegal or
attorney?" first and sends the answer as `profileType`, because there is no
account to read it from.

A demo is 20 questions in 20 minutes drawn across all four levels — it is
**not** a Beginner quiz and must not be presented as one.

item.name: Practice

request.description: `hasAccess` says whether this user’s subscription includes the office — that is the only paywall.
Derived from the content, so the EPO shows patents only and the EUIPO trade marks and designs only. Each level carries its question count and its time limit.

A theme with fewer than 20 questions returns `isShortSession: true` and the exact sentence to show: "This theme has 13 questions: this session has 13."

For a paralegal, a theme with fewer than 5 questions is left out entirely.
WIPO and the UPC are excluded: their theme lists are their own and cannot be compared with the others.
20 questions from one sheet. Time limit follows the level.
Across all four levels. Sending `level` as well is refused on purpose.
The whole office. Add `subject` to narrow it to one discipline.
At least two offices, and neither may be WIPO or the UPC.
Questions answered wrongly before and not yet answered correctly since. Returns 404 with a clear message when there are none.
Step order, 20 at a time, resuming where the user stopped. A session stops at the end of a level even if that is fewer than 20.
Returns the questions with `selectedKey` for whatever was already answered.
Scores it, updates the mistakes pool and advances the learning path. 7 right out of 20 is reported as 35%.
The full question-by-question breakdown.

item.description:
Figma: **practice section** (11 screens).

The flow is: office → discipline → level (or theme) → session. All seven
modes go through the same `POST /practice/session`; only `mode` and the
fields it needs change.

| mode | needs | pool |
|---|---|---|
| `by_level` | office, subject, level | one sheet |
| `by_theme` | office, subject, theme | that theme, all four levels |
| `random` | office (+ optional subject) | the whole office |
| `theme_across_offices` | subject, theme, offices[] | that theme in those offices |
| `review_mistakes` | optional office | what the user got wrong and has not since got right |
| `learning_path` | office, subject | Step order, resuming where they stopped |
| `demo` | office, profileType | the 20 demo questions |

A theme quiz never takes a level: it always runs across all four.

item.name: Progress

request.description: Completed sessions, newest first.
Where the user stands in each office + discipline they have started: `lastStepCompleted` out of `totalQuestions`.
How many questions the user got wrong and has not since got right, per office. Drives the "Review my mistakes" entry point.

item.description: Figma: **review section** (3 screens) and the Profile screens that show progress.

item.name: Subscription

request.description: The four plans with CHF prices, office counts and which choices each one expects. Render the Plans screen from this rather than hard-coding it.
`{ all, international, regional, national }`. The Track selection screen needs the regional and national groups.

**The endpoint that decides what to unlock.** `officeCodes` is the union of the offices of every plan held.

`needsOfficeSelection: true` means a plan is paid for but has no office chosen yet — send the user to the selection screen before anything else.
Call right after `purchasePackage()` or `restorePurchases()`. Returns the refreshed access, so you do not wait for the webhook.

Focus sends `{ "single": "CNIPA" }`. Track sends `{ "national": "...", "regional": "..." }` — WIPO comes with Track automatically, do not send it.

Allowed **once per billing period**; `canChangeOffices` on my-access says whether the button should be enabled.

item.description:
Figma: the subscription screens in **Demo quiz** and **Profile Section**.

**The purchase happens in your app**, through App Store / Google Play billing
with the RevenueCat SDK. This server never charges anyone — it tells you what
the user holds.

Call `Purchases.logIn()` with our Mongo user id so RevenueCat's
`app_user_id` matches, then call **Sync** after any purchase or restore.

Every report carries the office, the sheet and the Case_No of the question,
so the content team can find the exact row in the workbook. Those three are
read from the stored question — you only send the question and the comment.
